controls.section: 1.1 Implement strong password security measures
controls.description: Authentication is resistant to brute force attacks

controls.section: 1.1 Implement strong password security measures
controls.description: System generated initial passwords or activation codes shall be securely randomly generated and expire after a short period.

controls.section: 1.1 Implement strong password security measures
controls.description: Passwords shall be stored in a form that is resistant to offline attacks.

controls.section: 1.2 Disable any default accounts for public application access interfaces
controls.description: Default credentials shall not present on publicly exposed interfaces.

controls.section: 1.3 Out of band verifiers shall be random and not reused
controls.description: Out of band verifier shall expire in a reasonable timeframe.

controls.section: 1.3 Out of band verifiers shall be random and not reused
controls.description: Out of band verifier shall only be used once.

controls.section: 1.3 Out of band verifiers shall be random and not reused
controls.description: Out of band verifier shall be securely random

controls.section: 1.3 Out of band verifiers shall be random and not reused
controls.description: Out of band verifier shall be resistant to brute force attacks

controls.section: 2.1 URLs shall not expose authentication material
controls.description: The application shall not reveal passwords or session tokens in URL parameters. In cases where the application provides an API, the application shall prevent (or give developers an option) to prevent exposing sensitive information like API keys or session tokens within the URL query strings

controls.section: 2.2 Implement session invalidation on logout, user request, and password change
controls.description: Users shall have the ability to logout of the application. Logout or session expiration shall invalidate all stateful session tokens, including refresh tokens.

controls.section: 2.2 Implement session invalidation on logout, user request, and password change
controls.description: The application shall provide the option (or acts by default) to terminate all other active sessions, including stateful refresh tokens, after a successful password change (including change via password reset/recovery), and that this is effective across the application, federated login (if present), and any relying parties.

controls.section: 2.2 Implement session invalidation on logout, user request, and password change
controls.description: Non-revocable sateless authentication tokens must expire within 24 hours of being issued

controls.section: 2.3 Implement and secure application session tokens
controls.description: Cookie-based session tokens shall have the 'Secure' attribute set.

controls.section: 2.3 Implement and secure application session tokens
controls.description: Cookie-based session tokens shall have the 'HttpOnly' attribute set.

controls.section: 2.3 Implement and secure application session tokens
controls.description: The application shall use session tokens rather than static API secrets and keys, except with legacy implementations.

controls.section: 2.3 Implement and secure application session tokens
controls.description: Stateless session tokens shall use digital signatures, encryption, and other countermeasures to protect against tampering, enveloping, replay, null cipher, and key substitution attacks.

controls.section: 2.4 Protect sensitive account modifications
controls.description: Verify the application ensures a full, valid login session or requires re-authentication or secondary verification before allowing any sensitive transactions or account modifications.

controls.section: 3.1 Implement access control mechanisms to protect data and APIs
controls.description: The application shall enforce least privilege access control rules on a trusted service layer.

controls.section: 3.1 Implement access control mechanisms to protect data and APIs
controls.description: All user and data attributes and policy information used by access controls shall not be able to be manipulated by end users unless specifically authorized.

controls.section: 3.1 Implement access control mechanisms to protect data and APIs
controls.description: Access controls shall fail securely including when an exception occurs.

controls.section: 3.1 Implement access control mechanisms to protect data and APIs
controls.description: Sensitive resources shall be protected against Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) attacks targeting creation, reading, updating and deletion of records, such as creating or updating someone else's record, viewing everyone's records, or deleting all records.

controls.section: 3.1 Implement access control mechanisms to protect data and APIs
controls.description: The application or framework shall enforce a strong anti-CSRF mechanism to protect authenticated functionality, and effective anti-automation or anti-CSRF protects unauthenticated functionality.

controls.section: 3.1 Implement access control mechanisms to protect data and APIs
controls.description: Directory browsing shall be disabled unless deliberately desired.

controls.section: 3.2 Implement secure OAuth integrations to protect user data and prevent unauthorized access
controls.description: Application shall implement only secure and recommended OAuth 2.0 flows, such as the Authorization Code Flow or the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, while avoiding the use of deprecated flows like the Implicit Flow or the Resource Owner Password Credentials Flow.

controls.section: 3.2 Implement secure OAuth integrations to protect user data and prevent unauthorized access
controls.description: Ensure that the application securely validates the redirect_uri and state parameters during the OAuth 2.0 authorization process to prevent open redirect and CSRF vulnerabilities.

controls.section: 3.3 Application exposed administrative interfaces shall use appropriate multi-factor authentication.
controls.description: Application administrative interfaces shall use appropriate multi-factor authentication to prevent unauthorized use.

controls.section: 4.1 Protect data through strong cryptography
controls.description: Application shall enforce the use of TLS for all connections and default to TLS 1.2+. In cases where support for legacy clients is necessary, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 may be supported if mitigations are implemented to minimize the risk of downgrade attacks and known TLS exploits. Regardless of the TLS version in use, the application shall default to secure cipher suites and reject those with known vulnerabilities.

controls.section: 4.1 Protect data through strong cryptography
controls.description: Connections to and from the server shall use trusted TLS certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the server must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates. All others should be rejected.

controls.section: 4.1 Protect data through strong cryptography
controls.description: No instances of weak cryptography which meaningfully impact the confidentiality or integrity of confidential data.

controls.section: 4.1 Protect data through strong cryptography
controls.description: All cryptographic modules shall fail securely, and errors are handled in a way that does not enable Padding Oracle attacks.

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Protect against HTTP parameter pollution.

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: URL redirects and forwards are limited to allowlisted URLs or a warning is displayed when redirecting to untrusted content.

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Avoid the use of eval() or other dynamic code execution features. When there is no alternative, any user input is sanitized and sandboxed before being executed.

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Protect against template injection attacks by ensuring that any user input being included is sanitized or sandboxed.

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Prevent Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Protect against XPath or XML injection attacks

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Context-aware output escaping or sanitization protects against reflected, stored, and DOM based XSS.

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Protect against database injection attacks

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Protect against OS command injections

controls.section: 5.1 Implement validation & input sanitation
controls.description: Protect against local file inclusion or remote file inclusion attacks

controls.section: 5.2 Securely Handle Untrusted Files
controls.description: Protect against malicious file uploads by limiting uploads to expected file types and preventing direct execution of uploaded content.

controls.section: 6.1 Keep all components up to date
controls.description: The app only uses software components without known exploitable vulnerabilities.

controls.section: 6.2 Disable debug modes in production environments
controls.description: Disable debug modes in production environments

controls.section: 6.3 The origin header shall not be used for authentication of access control decisions
controls.description: The origin header shall not be used for authentication of access control decisions

controls.section: 6.4 Protect Application from Subdomain Takeover
controls.description: The application shall not be susceptible to subdomain takeovers.

controls.section: 6.5 Do not log credentials or payment details
controls.description: The application shall not log credentials or payment details. Session tokens shall only be stored in logs in an irreversible, hashed form.

controls.section: 6.6 Securely clear client storage during logout
controls.description: Browser storage is securely cleared during logout.

controls.section: 6.7 Securely store server-side secrets
controls.description: The application shall securely store access tokens, API keys, and other server-side secrets.
